matched_question.prompt: Compare a Process and a Thread, and explain common Inter-Process Communication (IPC) mechanisms.

transcripts.raw_spoken: A process is a running program with its own memory space. So one process cannot directly change another process's data. A thread is a unit of execution instead of a process, and all threads in that process share the same heap memory. Because of this, creating a thread and doing a context switch between threads is cheaper than doing it for processes. The risk is that shared memory can cause a race condition. So we protect it with a mutex or a semfor. For example, a web browser can run each tab as a separate process for isolation, while one tab uses several threads for rendering and network calls.

matched_question.prompt: Explain how a Hash Map handles collisions and the significance of the load factor.

transcripts.raw_spoken: A hash map stores key value pairs. A hash function converts the key into an integer, and that integer decides the bucket index in an array. So, look up in O of 1 on average. A collision happens when two different keys land in the same bucket. Chaining handles this by keeping a linked list in each bucket while open addressing probes for the next free slot. To keep performance good, the table tracks its load factor and resize when it gets too full. In the worst case, with many collisions, look up degrades to O of n.

The risk is that sharing memories can cause a race condition so we protect it with a bluetex or a sembaphos. For example, a web browser can run each step as a separate process of isolation.
